recipes.name: Pan-Seared Tilapia
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 tablespoon lemon juice, or to taste
1 teaspoon chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon chopped fresh thyme, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon chopped fresh thyme, or to taste

steps.text: Pat tilapia fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and ground black pepper.
Place flour in a shallow dish. Gently press each fillet into flour to coat; shake off any excess.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook tilapia fillets in the hot oil, in batches if necessary, until golden brown, about 4 minutes per side.

Brush tilapia with melted butter during the last minute of cooking. Cook until fish flakes easily with a fork and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Drizzle tilapia with lemon juice and garnish with parsley and thyme, if using. Serve with lemon wedges, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Pan-Seared Tilapia
raw_recipe.description: This easy pan-seared tilapia recipe cooks in just 15 minutes for tender, flaky fish finished with butter, lemon, and fresh herbs.

video.description: Tilapia is one of the most popular types of fish in the United States because it's cheap, plentiful, and easy to cook. In this video, learn how to prepare this fish the right way with an easy, 15-minute recipe for pan-seared tilapia that's packed with flavor. This simple method of cooking fish filets works wonders for anyone trying to put together a hurried weeknight dinner. Serve it with fresh steamed vegetables to complete the meal.

review.reviewBody: First of all, my fish looked like the picture which AMAZED me because although I'm not a beginner cook I tend to over batter fish. This was AMAZING. My fiance loved it! There are things I changed just to suit my tastes...(I am sure the original recipe would have been just as good.) I added onto the normal salt and pepper...Old Bay, garlic salt, more paprika, a little ground red pepper, onion powder and then I dusted it with flour. What helped me know that the pan was hot enough was something I learned from the Food Network. I just took a tiny pinch of flour and tossed it in the oil...if it started to cook or bubble...that's how you know it's ready for the fish. I did not use the extra unsalted butter. THIS WAS AWESOME! My fiance ate the whole thing before I could sit down! He said it was better than his mom's! :) He even told his mom about it! Thank you so much for this dish!
So simple and good! You can add whatever seasoning you like to the flour. (I used blackened seafood seasoning) I made a garlic-butter, parsley and lime sauce to go on top. yum.
Very good! The whole family enjoyed it. I added Old Bay, Garlic Salt, Onion Powder, Paprika, and Crushed Red Pepper to the flour before coating.
It came out better than I anticipated, I rarely use flour for breading fish. And, I've never fried Tilapia, always grilled or baked. Yummy!

As written we rated a 4 as we felt it needed a little more spice. The next batch we took the advice of others and added in Old Bay Seasoning and left out the butter as we felt in was not necessary. Yummy

Delicious recipe! I added the spices (garlic salt, pepper, crushed oregano) to the flour before I coated the fish as well, which reduced the spices I had to add directly to the fish. Also, instead of brushing the melted butter on top of the fish during cooking, I added about half a tablespoon to the olive oil, and then heated the two together before adding the fish, so the fish seared in the oil and butter. My fish did not need 4 minutes per side either, they were perfect at about 3 minutes a side. So yummy, cannot wait to make this again!

This was a wonderful way to prepare tilapia. We were very pleasantly suprised. I used "Blackened Seasoning Mix" from this site to season the tilapia, along with some salt. I skipped the butter to cut back on calories. We didn't miss it at all. I know this recipe will be making a repeat appearance at our dinner table!

Great! My hubby loves tilapia, but I could take it or leave it...but this recipe had me taking seconds! I substituted italian panko bread crumbs for the flour & it was perfect. Since no egg is used the panko didn't completely cover the fish, but added the perfect amount of texture and taste. Served this with a homemade tarter sauce, steamed carrots & sesame green beans...wonderful!

AWESOME! So light and wonderful. It went great with brown rice and broccoli. My husband loved it. I did add some lemon juice at the end, but otherwise I followed the recipe exactly. I will definitely make this again (and often!).

For such a simple method, very good! I used a bit of Old Bay along with the salt and pepper, and added a bit of butter to the olive oil rather than adding it on top at the end. Cooked about 4 minutes per side (tilapia was 'almost' defrosted, but maybe not quite all the way) and it came out perfect.

Super easy and turned out really well. I might have overcooked it a little, but the family still enjoyed it. Like others, I added the butter to the oil in the pan and I added just a touch of Old Bay to seasoning the fillets. Served with steamed broccoli and mashed sweet potatoes.
Super delicious! Made a few upgrades as noted by Susan (below…thank you Susan)

I love this recipe I love I love fish especially tilapia and cod. The only thing I did different with this recipe is I also drizzle just a little bit of lime juice along with the lemon more lemon juice than lime but the two combinations really stood out. At least my family loved it.
No changes
We added zucchini and carrots. Great weeknight dinner.

This recipe has been a staple in my house for a while. The first time ever making fish, I was so afraid. This looks like the picture. My family likes it a little darker so i juat cook it a few extra minutes. I also so not use the salt- my mother in law can not have the salt. Forget store bought fish fry during lent, just make this. It is phenomenal.
1st time frying talapia. It was very easy and good!
Perfect!
I really haven’t cared for Tilapia before but thought we’d give this one a try. Well, now I’m making it for the third time. It’s simple yet flavorful. I didn’t change anything and I wouldn’t.
I’m gluten free and used 1:1 GF flour and it was delicious! Easy, quick and yummy. Will be adding to my regular rotation.
